look_here_first: Look for a broad-leaved submerged pondweed with alternate two-ranked leaves and a persistent axillary stipule/prophyll, then confirm the emergent many-flowered spike.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: persistent open-sheath stipule/prophyll in the leaf axil

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: thin lanceolate to narrowly rectangular leaf blades with strong parallel venation and cross-bridges

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mostly emergent many-flowered spike on a long peduncle

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: four green sepal-like floral segments and four stamens

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Flexible submerged shoots arise from horizontal rhizomes; adventitious roots occur at nodes.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Leaves are alternate and two-ranked, petiolate, with a conspicuous persistent axillary prophyll/stipule; blades are thin, lanceolate to narrowly rectangular and strongly veined.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Terminal or axillary emergent spike on a long peduncle; flowers sessile and densely arranged.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Small one-seeded drupelet-like fruits, usually four in a whorl.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's San Marcos River frame shows the submerged growth form and broad pondweed leaves in local river context.
